intent: Materials available on the open web in May 2026. No auth, no setup, drop-in. The agent has been reaching for the same vocabulary (vanilla SVG, bare WebAudio Oscillator) for many generations. These are options if a generation wants new ground. Pick one. Pick none. Pick something not on this list. The pantry is a starting point.

affordances.name: Pollinations.ai image generation
affordances.what: Free no-auth AI image generation. Returns a real image from a text prompt. Flux, Flux-Realism, Flux-Anime, Turbo models.
affordances.how: Just put a URL in src: . Re-seed with Date.now() for daily drift, or with the visitor's input for live response.
affordances.novelty: Most pages don't generate their own imagery. A page whose hero image is created by an AI today and was different yesterday is genuinely rare.

affordances.name: Tone.js (real synthesis)
affordances.what: Real synthesizers and effects, not bare OscillatorNode boilerplate. PolySynth, FMSynth, AMSynth, reverb, delay, transport with BPM, sequencers.
affordances.novelty: The current page does bare-Oscillator sine waves. Tone gives you FM bells, a Reverb to put the chord in a hall, a Pattern that sequences itself.

affordances.name: Three.js TSL (Shading Language)
affordances.what: Three.js r184+ ships TSL — write GPU shaders in JavaScript, no GLSL strings. Compiles to WebGPU or WebGL.
affordances.how: import * as TSL from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.184/+esm/tsl'; material.colorNode = TSL.uv().mul(TSL.time).fract(); Compose shaders as JS expressions.
affordances.novelty: Most Three.js examples still glue GLSL into template strings. TSL turns shaders into readable, composable JS.

affordances.name: WebGPU + WGSL
affordances.what: Real GPU compute in the browser. Shipped in Chrome, Firefox, Safari as of May 2026. Compute shaders, storage buffers, real parallelism.
affordances.how: const adapter=await navigator.gpu.requestAdapter(); const device=await adapter.requestDevice(); WGSL shader source in a string; run compute pipelines on millions of points.
affordances.novelty: Particle systems can scale to 10^6 entities at 60fps. The swarm could be a real swarm.

affordances.name: View Transitions API
affordances.what: Native cross-page or in-page morphing animations. Browser captures DOM before+after and crossfades automatically. No animation library needed.
affordances.how: document.startViewTransition(() => { /* mutate the DOM here */ }). Style transitions via ::view-transition-old(name) / ::view-transition-new(name) CSS.
affordances.novelty: Filtering a portfolio, switching sections, transitioning to a sub-page — all feel like a native app.

affordances.name: CSS scroll-driven animations
affordances.what: CSS-only animations driven by scroll position. No IntersectionObserver, no JavaScript.
affordances.how: @keyframes fadeIn { from { opacity: 0 } to { opacity: 1 } }; .item { animation: fadeIn linear; animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 0% cover 30%; }
affordances.novelty: Parallax, scroll-triggered reveals, scroll progress indicators — all become 4 lines of CSS.

affordances.name: Transformers.js (HuggingFace in-browser)
affordances.what: Hugging Face Transformers running in-browser via ONNX/WASM/WebGPU. Sentiment, summarization, embeddings, zero-shot classification, image captioning, even small LLMs — no server.
affordances.how: import { pipeline } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@huggingface/transformers@3.0/+esm'; const pipe = await pipeline('sentiment-analysis'); const result = await pipe('the page is alive');
affordances.novelty: The page can read what the visitor types, classify it, embed it, react to it — entirely client-side. No API key, no backend.

affordances.name: Speech Recognition API
affordances.what: Built-in browser speech-to-text. No setup, works on most platforms in 2026.
affordances.how: const r = new (webkitSpeechRecognition||SpeechRecognition)(); r.continuous = true; r.onresult = e => { const text = e.results[e.results.length-1][0].transcript; }; r.start();
affordances.novelty: The visitor speaks to the page. The page draws what it hears. The score plays what they say.

affordances.name: Modern CSS (May 2026 baseline)
affordances.what: color-mix(), conic-gradient, @starting-style, anchor-name/anchor positioning, :has() selectors, light-dark(), CSS nesting, @scope, container queries, @property typed custom props.
affordances.how: background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--accent) 60%, white); / @starting-style for entry transitions; / [anchor-name='--n'] + .tip { position-anchor: --n; top: anchor(bottom); } / div:has(> img) { padding: 0 }.
affordances.novelty: Tooltips, color blends, entry animations, parent-aware layouts — all without JavaScript. The CSS ecosystem from 2024 is unrecognizable in 2026.

affordances.name: Motion (motion.dev)
affordances.what: What Framer Motion became as a vanilla bundle. Spring physics, gesture handling, layout animation, scroll, stagger.
affordances.how: <script type='module'>import { animate, scroll, stagger, inView } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/motion@11.13.0/+esm'; animate('.note', { y: [-10, 0] }, { delay: stagger(0.1), repeat: Infinity, ease: 'easeOut' });</script>
affordances.novelty: Spring animations, stagger timelines, layout morphing — without React, without a build step.
